item.title: Sober (Curious) Monthly Coffee Walk — Sun Sep 13, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Lose The Booze Crew (20-40s) Hi friends!! Come join us for our monthly coffee walk around River Arts District.
**We'll be doing 3-4miles and leave promptly at 10:10am. Route will be same as last time, over Haywood bridge, then up to former French Broad park, turn around back up to Craven St bridge, and back to Ultra (there is active construction where French Broad Park used to be). Arrive on time or get left behind.** 🫣
**Important**- *Ultra's parking lot is tiny, please do not park there!!!* You can find plenty of parking on Lyman St, Clingman Ave or the gravel lot for Wedge (it’s now a paid lot)
**Gentle Reminder:** This isn't a 12-step, recovery group or dating mixer, just some people hanging out without the booze.
If your plans change, please update your RSVP status as soon as possible.
Well behaved doggos are welcome but keep in mind they won't be allowed inside the coffee shop.
Can't wait to see your beautiful faces 🤗!!
Source: Asheville Lose The Booze Crew

item.title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall — Tue Sep 15, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat — Tue Sep 22, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Autumn Mind-Body Wellness Retreat with Jenne Sluder Tuesday, September 22 | 10 am – 4pm Register Here!

item.description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum — Sat Oct 3, 9:30 AM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed.
